title: Atomic Emission Spectrum Line Visualizer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that visualizes atomic emission spectra as colored spectral lines in a 3D scene. The scene simulates how excited electrons in atoms emit photons at specific wavelengths when transitioning between energy levels.

## Scene Setup
- Black background (0x000000) to simulate a dark lab environment.
- Orthographic or perspective camera looking at a horizontal spectral band.
- A long rectangular 3D slab (the 'spectral plate', width ~20 units along X, height ~2 units along Y, depth ~0.2) centered at origin, colored dark gray (0x111111). This represents the detector/film.
- Above the spectral plate, render thin vertical rectangular planes (height ~3 units, width proportional to line intensity) representing individual emission lines. Each line is a MeshBasicMaterial colored according to its wavelength.
- Add a 3D atom model above-left of the spectral plate: a small sphere (nucleus, gold color) with 2-3 torus rings (orbits, white wireframe) tilted at different angles, slowly rotating.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.3) and one point light near the atom model.

## Element Data (hardcoded)
Support exactly 4 elements selectable by the user:
1. Hydrogen (H): lines at 410nm (violet), 434nm (blue-violet), 486nm (cyan-blue), 656nm (red). Balmer series.
2. Helium (He): lines at 388nm (deep violet), 447nm (blue), 502nm (green), 588nm (yellow), 668nm (red).
3. Neon (Ne): lines at 540nm (green), 585nm (yellow), 603nm (orange), 640nm (red-orange), 693nm (deep red), 703nm (deep red).
4. Sodium (Na): lines at 498nm (cyan-green), 515nm (green), 568nm (yellow-green), 589nm (yellow, the famous doublet — render two lines at 589.0 and 589.6), 616nm (orange).

## Wavelength-to-Color Mapping
Implement a function wavelengthToColor(nm) that converts a wavelength (380-750nm) to an approximate RGB color. Use a standard visible spectrum approximation algorithm. Lines outside 380-750nm should not be rendered.

## Spectral Line Positioning
Map wavelength range 380nm-750nm linearly to X positions on the spectral plate from left (-10) to right (+10). Each emission line is a vertical plane placed at the corresponding X position, sitting on top of the spectral plate.

## Line Intensity
Each line should have an 'intensity' property (0.3 to 1.0). The line's material opacity and emissive brightness should reflect this. Hydrogen 656nm has intensity 1.0, others vary. Store intensities in the element data.

## User Interactions
1. DOM Buttons: Four buttons labeled 'H', 'He', 'Ne', 'Na' at the top of the screen. Clicking one selects that element and updates the spectral lines. The active button should have a highlighted border (2px solid #00ffff).
2. Keyboard 1-4: Press keys 1, 2, 3, 4 to select H, He, Ne, Na respectively (same as buttons).
3. Hover Interaction: When the mouse hovers over a spectral line (use Raycaster), that line should glow brighter (increase emissive intensity by 2x) and a floating HTML tooltip div should appear near the cursor showing 'λ = XXXnm' and the energy in eV (E = 1240/λ where λ in nm gives eV). The tooltip disappears when not hovering any line.
4. Animate Transition: When switching elements, old lines should fade out (opacity 0 over 500ms) and new lines fade in (opacity 0 to target over 500ms). Track animation state.
5. Zoom Control: A DOM slider (range input) labeled 'Zoom' that controls camera zoom from 0.5x to 3.0x. Default 1.0x.
6. Toggle Wavelength Labels: A checkbox labeled 'Show Labels'. When checked, small CSS2DRenderer-style labels (or sprite text) appear below each spectral line showing its wavelength. When unchecked, labels are hidden. Default: unchecked.
7. Energy Level Diagram: On the right side of the screen, render a simple SVG or canvas-based energy level diagram showing horizontal lines for energy levels and arrows for the transitions of the currently selected element. Update when element changes.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields, updated every frame:
- selectedElement: string ('H', 'He', 'Ne', 'Na')
- lineCount: number of currently visible spectral lines for the selected element
- lineWavelengths: sorted array of wavelength numbers (nm) for current element
- linePositions: array of {wavelength, x} objects mapping each line to its X position on the spectral plate
- hoveredLine: wavelength number of currently hovered line, or null
- hoveredEnergy: energy in eV of hovered line (rounded to 4 decimal places), or null
- zoomLevel: current zoom multiplier (number)
- labelsVisible: boolean
- animating: boolean (true during fade transitions)
- atomRotation: current Y rotation of the atom model orbits in radians
- cameraPositionZ: camera z position
- lineIntensities: array of {wavelength, intensity} for current element
- energyLevels: number of energy levels shown in the diagram for current element
- tooltipVisible: boolean (whether tooltip div is currently displayed)

## Physics / Chemistry Constraints
- Wavelength-to-position mapping must be strictly linear: x = -10 + (wavelength - 380) / (750 - 380) * 20
- Energy calculation: E = 1240 / wavelength (eV), must be accurate to 4 decimal places
- All wavelengths must be in the visible range 380-750nm
- Line positions must be sorted left to right (increasing wavelength = increasing X)
- Zoom must clamp between 0.5 and 3.0

## Visual Polish
- Add a subtle bloom/glow effect on the spectral lines using additive blending or emissive materials.
- The atom model orbits should rotate continuously.
- Smooth CSS transitions on buttons and tooltip.
